injuries.name: Javontae Jean-Baptiste
injuries.shortComment: Jean-Baptiste (pectoral) will be sidelined for Monday's clash against the 49ers, Tashan Reed of The Washington Post reports.
injuries.longComment: Jean-Baptiste didn't practice at all this week, so it's not a surprise that he won't play Monday. Per Reed, head coach Dan Quinn expects rookie Joshua Josephs to see more playing time Week 6, with both Jean-Baptiste and Charles Omenihu (groin/ankle) sidelined.

injuries.name: Charles Omenihu
injuries.shortComment: Omenihu (groin/ankle) has been ruled out for Monday's Week 6 matchup against San Francisco, Tashan Reed of The Washington Post reports.
injuries.longComment: This will be Omehihu's second straight absence after he was injured early against Indianapolis in Week 4. The Commanders are on bye next week, so the veteran defensive end will look to return in Week 8 against Philadelphia. Javon Kinlaw (ankle/knee) is questionable for Monday's contest, so Washington may need to lean more on Shy Tuttle and/or Deatrich Wise.

injuries.name: Jeremy McNichols
injuries.shortComment: McNichols (quadriceps) is questionable for Monday night's game against the 49ers.
injuries.longComment: McNichols was a full practice participant this week but remains on injured reserve, though the Commanders could still choose to activate him ahead of Monday night's contest. With Jacory Croskey-Merritt (foot) out, the Commanders could use McNichols as depth alongside Rachaad White and Austin Ekeler.

injuries.name: Jeremy Reaves
injuries.shortComment: Reaves (rib) doesn't carry an injury designation into Monday night's game against the 49ers.
injuries.longComment: Reaves was limited in practice all week but is good to go versus San Francisco. He's also dealt with a finger injury lately but has yet to miss a game this season. Reaves has recorded 34 tackles (20 solo) and a pair of pass breakups on 92.5 percent of the defensive snaps through five games.

injuries.name: Treylon Burks
injuries.shortComment: Burks (shoulder) doesn't have a designation for Monday's game in San Francisco.
injuries.longComment: Burks practiced in a limited capacity during the entirety of Week 6 prep due to a shoulder issue, but it won't stop him from being available Monday. Fellow WR Stefon Diggs (hamstring) is listed as questionable, and if he's inhibited or sidelined this week, Burks will stand to benefit in the Commanders' passing game. In four contests this season, Burks has notched five catches (on 11 targets) for 86 yards and two touchdowns.

injuries.name: Austin Ekeler
injuries.shortComment: Ekeler (chest) does not carry an injury designation into Monday's game against the 49ers.
injuries.longComment: Ekeler was limited in practice all week due to a chest injury, but he's done enough to fade an injury tag for Monday Night Football. With Jacory Croskey-Merritt (groin) already ruled out, Ekeler and Rachaad White are both expected to lead the Commanders' backfield for Week 6 against a 49ers defense that has given up only three rushing touchdowns across five regular-season games.

injuries.name: Rachaad White
injuries.shortComment: White (shoulder) doesn't have a designation for Monday's game at San Francisco.
injuries.longComment: Despite ending Week 6 prep with back-to-back limited practices due to a shoulder injury, White will be available to the Commanders backfield Monday along with Austin Ekeler (chest). With Jacory Croskey-Merritt (groin) ruled out, White and Ekeler are the candidates to lead Washington's backfield this week. On the season, White had 39 touches for 171 yards from scrimmage and one receiving TD in four appearances.

injuries.name: Stefon Diggs
injuries.shortComment: Diggs (hamstring) is listed as questionable for Monday's game against San Francisco.
injuries.longComment: Diggs ended the week with back-to-back limited practices, which was enough for him to draw the questionable tag for Monday Night Football. Diggs did not play in Week 5 against the Giants, but if he's cleared to play against the 49ers, then it would be the first time that he, Terry McLaurin and Jayden Daniels are on the field together since Week 2 against the Cowboys. If Diggs does not play, then Antonio Williams and Treylon Burks would both operate in elevated roles offensively behind McLaurin.

injuries.name: Terry McLaurin
injuries.shortComment: McLaurin (hamstring) does not have an injury designation ahead of Monday's game against the 49ers.
injuries.longComment: McLaurin logged an LP-DNP-LP practice log while tending to a lingering hamstring injury, but he has been given the green light to play in Monday night's game. The Commanders could also have Stefon Diggs (hamstring) back in action, and in that case, Washington would have McLaurin, Diggs and Jayden Daniels share the field for the first time since Week 2 against the Cowboys. McLaurin has a 14-203-1 receiving line on 26 targets across four regular-season games.

injuries.name: Marcus Mariota
injuries.shortComment: Mariota (knee) has been ruled out for Monday's game against the 49ers, Tashan Reed of The Washington Post reports.
injuries.longComment: As expected, Mariota will miss a second consecutive game due to a sprained MCL in his right knee, which he picked up during the Commanders' Week 4 loss to the Colts in London. Rookie seventh-rounder Athan Kaliakmanis will once again serve as Washington's backup quarterback behind Jayden Daniels for Monday night's game. The Commanders are on a bye for Week 7, so Mariota could be back in action for Week 8 against the Eagles on Sunday, Nov. 1.

injuries.name: Jacory Croskey-Merritt
injuries.shortComment: Croskey-Merritt (groin) has been ruled out for Monday night's game against the 49ers, Tashan Reed of The Washington Post reports.
injuries.longComment: Croskey-Merritt was unable to practice all week due to a groin injury, and he's now been officially ruled out for Monday night's game. The statuses of Rachaad White (shoulder) and Austin Ekeler (chest) will be known once the Commanders announce their injury designations on Saturday's practice report. Washington is on a bye for Week 7, so Croskey-Merritt will have more time to recover from his injury before the Commanders' Week 8 tilt against the Eagles on Sunday, Nov. 1.

injuries.name: Jordan Magee
injuries.shortComment: Magee (hamstring) was designated to return from injured reserve Thursday.
injuries.longComment: Magee suffered a hamstring injury in the Week 1 loss to Philadelphia. As a result, he was placed on injured reserve and missed the last four contests. Magee can be activated any time in the next 21 days, meaning there's a chance he will suit up Monday night against the 49ers.

injuries.name: Antonio Williams
injuries.shortComment: Williams hauled in all three of his targets for 31 yards and added a two-yard punt return during the Commanders' 27-27 tie with the Giants on Sunday.
injuries.longComment: Williams didn't see a target from Jayden Daniels until early in the third quarter, when the duo connected on a 17-yard pass on the first of a five-play drive that ended with a 38-yard rushing touchdown by Daniels. Williams finished third on the Commanders in both receptions and receiving yards behind Terry McLaurin and Chig Okonkwo, and the rookie wideout has a 15-155-1 receiving line on 22 targets through five regular-season games. The Commanders have a tough Week 6 road tilt against the undefeated 49ers on Monday Night Football.

injuries.name: Van Jefferson
injuries.shortComment: Jefferson reverted to the Commanders' practice squad Monday.
injuries.longComment: Jefferson was elevated for the first time this season ahead of Sunday's 27-27 tie with the Giants. He logged three snaps on offense without drawing a target or touch while adding 13 snaps on special teams. Whether Jefferson gets elevated again Week 6 versus San Francisco may depend on whether Stefon Diggs is able to return from a hamstring injury.

injuries.name: Chig Okonkwo
injuries.shortComment: Okonkwo caught four of six targets for 60 yards during Sunday's 27-27 tie against the Giants.
injuries.longComment: Okonkwo had his most productive day of the year, finishing tied for the team lead in receptions with wide receiver Terry McLaurin, while his six targets led the way for Washington. The tight end now has caught eight of 13 targets for 81 yards over three contests this season, and he'll look to continue building chemistry with starting quarterback Jayden Daniels moving forward.

injuries.name: Drew Stevens
injuries.shortComment: Stevens made both of his field-goal attempts and went 1-for-2 on extra-point tries during the Commanders' 27-27 tie with the Giants on Sunday.
injuries.longComment: Stevens missed his first kick of the game, a point-after attempt early in the first quarter, before connecting on field goals from 28 and 40 yards in the second period. Stevens has connected on two field goals in each of his last four outings and is 9-for-11 on field-goal attempts and 8-for-11 on extra-point tries through five games. The Commanders will hit the road for Week 6 against the 49ers on Monday, Oct. 19.

injuries.name: Jayden Daniels
injuries.shortComment: Daniels (elbow) completed 17 of 25 passes for 199 yards, no touchdowns and no interceptions while rushing nine times for 103 yards and two touchdowns in Sunday's 27-27 tie against the Giants. He also threw a successful two-point conversion.
injuries.longComment: Daniels wasn't afraid to run in his return from a two-game absence due to a dislocated left elbow. He scored second-half rushing touchdowns of 38 and 26 yards, the latter of which Daniels followed up with a two-point conversion to Terry McLaurin to give the Commanders a 14-point lead with 11:05 left in the fourth quarter. The Giants proceeded to erase that deficit and force OT, where Daniels drove the Commanders down to the Giants' 24-yard line with 55 seconds remaining, but Washington remarkably failed to get a game-winning field-goal attempt off, as the Commanders ran the clock down and then failed to stop the clock when Daniels went down inbounds on their final offensive play. The bizarre ending overshadows what was otherwise an encouraging performance from Daniels, who made it through the game without any physical setbacks and is set to start in Week 6 against the 49ers.
